transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I came in because... well, I just keep thinking it would be better if I didn't wake up in the morning. It's been heavy on my mind. Sometimes I honestly feel like dying would be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family, and to my crew at work. I just don't know what else to do anymore.
Are you thinking about killing yourself right now?

Not right this exact minute, no. But... like I was just saying, the thought of just not waking up tomorrow is constantly there. I don't have a specific plan to do it right now, but I just really feel like dying is the only fair punishment left for what I've put my family through, and the guys on my crew. I just want it to be over.
Do you believe you have actually done something so bad that you deserve to die?

Yes. I really do. I just keep thinking that I'm the reason my husband got worse. And at work... my crew lost work because of me, and clients' homes got messed up. It's like I just poisoned everything I touched. So, yeah, I feel like I deserve whatever happens to me.
Has anyone told you that you are not actually responsible for those things, but you still believe with certainty that you are?

Yes, they have. My husband tries to tell me that, and some of the guys. But... I know I am. Because even when I'm not crying or just stuck down in bed, I know what's going on. 

I am absolutely certain that the homeowners and the suppliers are tracking me. They use the floor patterns we lay down, the text messages, the permit calls... they use all of that to track whether I'm ruining the jobs on purpose. People try to tell me that's not happening, but no one can talk me out of it. I just know they're doing it.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually high, euphoric, or extremely energized for several days in a row?

No... no, I haven't. I don't really get energized or... euphoric. Honestly, I'm usually just exhausted. I've never had a time where I felt really high or full of energy for days like you're saying. It's pretty much just the opposite.
Have there been times when you were not feeling depressed but still believed people were tracking you?

Yes. Actually, there was a stretch... maybe a few weeks, where I was doing a bit better. I was getting up out of bed, eating a little more normally, and I wasn't crying all day long. But even then, I still heard the voice when I was at work, and I was still completely convinced that the clients and suppliers were tracking me. So, yeah, it didn't go away even when my mood lifted a bit.
